# Deploying Wuxia for WordPress

Follow this guide from top to bottom and you end with a site whose pages load **and whose episodes play**. Every command is meant to be copied as-is; replace only the values in `ALL_CAPS` (such as `YOUR_DOMAIN`). Prefer a guide at your side? An AI assistant can walk you through it: see [Deploy with an AI assistant](#6-deploy-with-an-ai-assistant).

- [Before you start: pick your hosting](#1-before-you-start-pick-your-hosting)
- [Path A: a new Ubuntu server](#2-path-a-a-new-ubuntu-server-recommended)
- [Path B: a hosting panel that runs nginx](#3-path-b-a-hosting-panel-that-runs-nginx)
- [Path C: a server that already runs nginx](#4-path-c-a-server-that-already-runs-nginx)
- [Path D: Docker with Nginx Proxy Manager](#5-path-d-docker-with-nginx-proxy-manager)
- [Deploy with an AI assistant](#6-deploy-with-an-ai-assistant)
- [Cloudflare](#7-cloudflare)
- [Install the theme and plugin](#8-install-the-theme-and-plugin)
- [Check that video plays](#9-check-that-video-plays)
- [Troubleshooting](#10-troubleshooting)
- [Updates and backups](#11-updates-and-backups)

## How video reaches a viewer

```
viewer ──▶ Cloudflare ──▶ nginx ──▶ WordPress checks the signed /media/ link, names the file
                            │
                            └──▶ nginx fetches the file from your storage (R2, S3, Telegram, …) and streams it
```

WordPress never streams video itself, and viewers never see your storage address. This needs **two nginx rules** ([`server/nginx-wuxia-media.conf`](server/nginx-wuxia-media.conf)). Without them the site works but every episode answers `501 Media is served through nginx`.

## 1. Before you start: pick your hosting

| Your hosting | Pages | Video | Follow |
|---|---|---|---|
| A VPS or dedicated server you can `ssh` into (Ubuntu 24.04) | Yes | Yes | [Path A](#2-path-a-a-new-ubuntu-server-recommended) |
| A panel that runs nginx and accepts custom nginx config (CloudPanel, RunCloud, SpinupWP, GridPane, Plesk with nginx) | Yes | Yes | [Path B](#3-path-b-a-hosting-panel-that-runs-nginx) |
| A server where you already run WordPress on nginx | Yes | Yes | [Path C](#4-path-c-a-server-that-already-runs-nginx) |
| A server with Docker, where you want [Nginx Proxy Manager](https://nginxproxymanager.com) to handle domains and HTTPS certificates | Yes | Yes | [Path D](#5-path-d-docker-with-nginx-proxy-manager) |
| Shared hosting, cPanel, Apache or LiteSpeed | Yes | **No** | Move to one of the rows above |

How to tell what an existing site runs: in a terminal, `curl -sI https://YOUR_DOMAIN/xmlrpc.php`. Behind Cloudflare the `server:` header always says `cloudflare`, so ask your host, or look in its control panel for "nginx" or "Apache/LiteSpeed".

A server with 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM and 40 GB of disk is plenty to start. The disk also holds the video cache (20 GB by default).

## 2. Path A: a new Ubuntu server (recommended)

Log in as a user with `sudo` on a fresh **Ubuntu 24.04**.

### 2.1 Firewall and packages

```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt -y upgrade
sudo ufw allow OpenSSH
sudo ufw allow 80,443/tcp
sudo ufw --force enable

sudo apt -y install nginx mariadb-server \
  php8.3-fpm php8.3-mysql php8.3-curl php8.3-xml php8.3-mbstring \
  php8.3-zip php8.3-gd php8.3-intl unzip curl
```

### 2.2 Database

```bash
sudo mysql_secure_installation   # answer Y to every question
sudo mysql -e "CREATE DATABASE wuxia CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
CREATE USER 'wuxia'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'A_STRONG_DB_PASSWORD';
GRANT ALL ON wuxia.* TO 'wuxia'@'localhost'; FLUSH PRIVILEGES;"
```

### 2.3 WordPress files

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /var/www/wuxia
curl -sL https://wordpress.org/latest.tar.gz | sudo tar -xz -C /var/www/wuxia --strip-components=1
sudo chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/wuxia
```

### 2.4 The Cloudflare origin certificate

Cloudflare talks to your server over HTTPS with a free certificate that lasts 15 years.

1. In Cloudflare: **SSL/TLS → Origin Server → Create Certificate** (keep the defaults) → **Create**.
2. On the server, paste the two blocks it shows:

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /etc/nginx/certs
sudo nano /etc/nginx/certs/origin.pem   # paste "Origin Certificate", save
sudo nano /etc/nginx/certs/origin.key   # paste "Private Key", save
sudo chmod 600 /etc/nginx/certs/origin.key
```

### 2.5 nginx: visitor IPs behind Cloudflare

Without this every visitor looks like a Cloudflare address, and the media rate limit would slow everyone together.

```bash
{ for ip in $(curl -s https://www.cloudflare.com/ips-v4) $(curl -s https://www.cloudflare.com/ips-v6); do
    echo "set_real_ip_from $ip;"; done
  echo "real_ip_header CF-Connecting-IP;"; } | sudo tee /etc/nginx/conf.d/cloudflare-realip.conf
```

### 2.6 nginx: the media rules

```bash
sudo curl -sL -o /etc/nginx/wuxia-media.conf \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wuxia-KH/wuxia-press-published-/main/server/nginx-wuxia-media.conf
sudo mkdir -p /var/cache/nginx/wuxia && sudo chown -R www-data /var/cache/nginx/wuxia
```

Part 1 of that file belongs inside `http { }` and part 2 inside `server { }`. Split it into two files:

```bash
sudo sed -n '/PART 1: http/,/PART 2: server/p' /etc/nginx/wuxia-media.conf | sudo tee /etc/nginx/conf.d/wuxia-media-http.conf >/dev/null
sudo sed -n '/PART 2: server/,$p' /etc/nginx/wuxia-media.conf | sudo tee /etc/nginx/snippets/wuxia-media-server.conf >/dev/null
```

The file already points at Ubuntu 24.04's PHP (`unix:/run/php/php8.3-fpm.sock`) and CA bundle, so nothing needs changing on this path.

### 2.7 nginx: the site

```bash
sudo tee /etc/nginx/sites-available/wuxia >/dev/null <<'EOF'
server {
	listen 80;
	server_name YOUR_DOMAIN www.YOUR_DOMAIN;
	return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}

server {
	listen 443 ssl;
	http2 on;
	server_name YOUR_DOMAIN www.YOUR_DOMAIN;
	ssl_certificate     /etc/nginx/certs/origin.pem;
	ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/certs/origin.key;

	root /var/www/wuxia;
	index index.php;
	client_max_body_size 32m;
	server_tokens off;

	# Video (Wuxia). Its ^~ locations take priority over the rules below.
	include snippets/wuxia-media-server.conf;

	location ~ /\. { deny all; }
	location = /xmlrpc.php { deny all; }
	location ~* ^/wp-content/uploads/.*\.php$ { deny all; }

	location / {
		try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?$args;
	}

	location ~ \.php$ {
		try_files $uri =404;
		include fastcgi_params;
		fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $document_root$fastcgi_script_name;
		fastcgi_pass unix:/run/php/php8.3-fpm.sock;
	}

	location ~* \.(css|js|webp|avif|jpg|jpeg|png|svg|ttf|woff2)$ {
		expires 30d;
		access_log off;
	}
}
EOF
sudo sed -i 's/YOUR_DOMAIN/example.com/g' /etc/nginx/sites-available/wuxia   # ← your domain here
sudo ln -sf /etc/nginx/sites-available/wuxia /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/wuxia
sudo rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

`nginx -t` must print `syntax is ok` and `test is successful`. If not, see [Troubleshooting](#10-troubleshooting).

Now set up [Cloudflare](#7-cloudflare), then open `https://YOUR_DOMAIN` and run the WordPress installer (database `wuxia`, user `wuxia`, the password from 2.2).

## 3. Path B: a hosting panel that runs nginx

Create the WordPress site in the panel as usual, then add the rules as **custom nginx configuration**:

| Panel | Where |
|---|---|
| CloudPanel | Site → **Vhost** (edit the file directly) |
| RunCloud | Web Application → **NGINX Config** → add a config of type `location.main-before` and one of type `http` |
| SpinupWP | Site → **Custom Nginx Config** (or `/etc/nginx/sites-available/<site>/server/` over SSH) |
| GridPane | `/var/www/<site>/nginx/` includes over SSH |
| Plesk | Domain → **Apache & nginx Settings** → *Additional nginx directives*, with "Proxy mode" **off** |

Then:

1. From [`nginx-wuxia-media.conf`](server/nginx-wuxia-media.conf), put **part 1** where the panel accepts `http`-level config. If it has none, ask your host to add those two lines (`limit_req_zone …` and `proxy_cache_path …`); both are harmless to other sites.
2. Put **part 2** in the site's server block.
3. Change `fastcgi_pass` to the one the panel already uses for PHP. Look for `fastcgi_pass` in the site's vhost; copy that value exactly.
4. Create the cache folder, or ask your host to: `mkdir -p /var/cache/nginx/wuxia`, owned by nginx's user.
5. Save; the panel reloads nginx. If it reports an error, the message names the line.

## 4. Path C: a server that already runs nginx

1. Download [`nginx-wuxia-media.conf`](server/nginx-wuxia-media.conf).
2. **Part 1** inside `http { }` (usually a new file in `/etc/nginx/conf.d/`).
3. **Part 2** inside the site's `server { }`, next to its other `location` blocks.
4. Lines marked `CHANGE`: set `fastcgi_pass` to the same value as your `location ~ \.php$` block; on RHEL, Alma or Rocky set the CA bundle to `/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt`.
5. `sudo mkdir -p /var/cache/nginx/wuxia && sudo chown -R www-data /var/cache/nginx/wuxia` (the user is `nginx` on RHEL-family systems).
6. If the site is behind Cloudflare, add the visitor-IP file from [2.5](#25-nginx-visitor-ips-behind-cloudflare).
7. `sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx`

## 5. Path D: Docker with Nginx Proxy Manager

[Nginx Proxy Manager](https://nginxproxymanager.com) gives you a web panel for domains and free HTTPS certificates. It only forwards traffic, so the Wuxia media rules live in a small nginx container behind it:

```
viewer ──▶ Cloudflare (optional) ──▶ Nginx Proxy Manager (HTTPS) ──▶ nginx + Wuxia media rules ──▶ WordPress (PHP-FPM) ──▶ MariaDB
```

Everything runs in Docker from one folder. This setup was tested end to end: an episode's playlist and video segments played through Nginx Proxy Manager, from nginx's cache on the second request.

### 5.1 Docker and the firewall

On a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 (Debian works too):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh
sudo ufw allow OpenSSH
sudo ufw allow 80,443/tcp
sudo ufw --force enable
```

### 5.2 The files

```bash
mkdir -p ~/wuxia/nginx && cd ~/wuxia
RAW=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wuxia-KH/wuxia-press-published-/main/server
curl -sLo docker-compose.yml "$RAW/nginx-proxy-manager/docker-compose.yml"
curl -sLo nginx/site.conf "$RAW/nginx-proxy-manager/nginx/site.conf"
curl -sLo nginx/nginx-wuxia-media.conf "$RAW/nginx-wuxia-media.conf"
sed -n '/PART 1: http/,/PART 2: server/p' nginx/nginx-wuxia-media.conf > nginx/wuxia-media-http.conf
sed -n '/PART 2: server/,$p' nginx/nginx-wuxia-media.conf | sed 's#unix:/run/php/php8.3-fpm.sock#wordpress:9000#' > nginx/wuxia-media-server.conf
for ip in $(curl -s https://www.cloudflare.com/ips-v4) $(curl -s https://www.cloudflare.com/ips-v6); do
  echo "set_real_ip_from $ip;"; done > nginx/cloudflare.conf
ls nginx
```

`ls` lists `cloudflare.conf`, `nginx-wuxia-media.conf`, `site.conf`, `wuxia-media-http.conf` and `wuxia-media-server.conf`. The Cloudflare file lets nginx see visitors' real addresses behind Cloudflare; without Cloudflare it does nothing.

### 5.3 Passwords, then start

This puts random database passwords into `docker-compose.yml`; you never need to type them.

```bash
sed -i "s/A_STRONG_DB_PASSWORD/$(openssl rand -hex 16)/g; s/A_STRONG_ROOT_PASSWORD/$(openssl rand -hex 16)/" docker-compose.yml
sudo docker compose up -d
sudo docker compose ps
```

All four services (`npm`, `db`, `wordpress`, `web`) show `Up` (or `running`).

### 5.4 Open the Nginx Proxy Manager panel

The panel (port 81) listens only on the server itself, so it is never exposed to the internet. From **your own computer**, open a tunnel:

```bash
ssh -L 8181:127.0.0.1:81 YOUR_USER@YOUR_SERVER_IP
```

Keep that window open and browse to `http://localhost:8181`. On the first visit, create the admin account (name, email, password). Older versions instead show a login: `admin@example.com` / `changeme`, then ask you to change both.

### 5.5 The proxy host

1. In Cloudflare (or your DNS), point `YOUR_DOMAIN` and `www` at the server's IP (see [Cloudflare](#7-cloudflare)).
2. In the panel: **Hosts → Proxy Hosts → Add Proxy Host**, **Details** tab:

   | Field | Value |
   |---|---|
   | Domain Names | `YOUR_DOMAIN` and `www.YOUR_DOMAIN` |
   | Scheme | `http` |
   | Forward Hostname / IP | `web` |
   | Forward Port | `80` |
   | Cache Assets | off |
   | Block Common Exploits | off (not needed: WordPress and nginx check every media link themselves) |
   | Websockets Support | off |

3. **SSL** tab: **Request a new SSL Certificate**, turn on **Force SSL** and **HTTP/2 Support**, agree to the terms, **Save**.
   - With Cloudflare's orange cloud on, tick **Use a DNS Challenge**, choose **Cloudflare**, and paste an API token that can edit DNS for the zone (Cloudflare → My Profile → API Tokens → *Edit zone DNS* template).
   - Or use a Cloudflare Origin Certificate: **SSL Certificates → Add SSL Certificate → Custom**, upload the certificate and key from Cloudflare's **SSL/TLS → Origin Server**, then pick it on the proxy host's SSL tab.

### 5.6 WordPress

Open `https://YOUR_DOMAIN`: the WordPress installer asks only for a site title and your admin account (the database is already connected). Then continue with [Install the theme and plugin](#8-install-the-theme-and-plugin).

On this path `wp-config.php` settings go in `docker-compose.yml`, under the `wordpress` service's `WORDPRESS_CONFIG_EXTRA`, one `define` per line after the one already there; then run `sudo docker compose up -d`.

## 6. Deploy with an AI assistant

AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot can read this guide and walk you through it, one step at a time. It is published for them as plain text at [`llms-full.txt`](https://wuxia-kh.github.io/wuxia-press-published-/llms-full.txt), with an index at [`llms.txt`](https://wuxia-kh.github.io/wuxia-press-published-/llms.txt).

Copy this into the assistant and fill in the brackets:

```text
Help me deploy "Wuxia for WordPress" so that its pages load and its episodes play.
First read the deployment guide and follow it exactly:
https://wuxia-kh.github.io/wuxia-press-published-/llms-full.txt

My setup:
- Hosting: [a new Ubuntu 24.04 VPS | a hosting panel called ... | a server already running nginx | Docker with Nginx Proxy Manager]
- Domain: [example.com]
- Cloudflare in front: [yes | no]

Give me one step at a time with the exact command, and tell me what I should see
before I go on. If something fails, use the guide's troubleshooting table.
Never ask me to paste passwords, API keys or tokens into this chat.
```

- **Assistants that can run commands** on your server (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and similar) can follow the guide directly. Read each command before you approve it.
- **Keep secrets out of the chat.** The guide generates passwords on the server; an assistant never needs to see them.
- **The guide is the reference.** If an assistant's advice disagrees with it, trust the guide, especially the nginx rules.

## 7. Cloudflare

1. Add the domain; create `A` records for `@` and `www` pointing at the server, **Proxied** (orange cloud).
2. **SSL/TLS → Overview → Full (strict).** Never *Flexible*: it loops wp-admin redirects.
3. **Caching → Cache Rules → Create rule** "Wuxia media": *URI Path starts with* `/media/` → **Eligible for cache**, Edge TTL **Use cache-control header if present**. Segments then come from Cloudflare instead of your server.
4. **Caching → Cache Rules**: bypass cache for `/wp-admin`, `/wp-login.php` and `/wp-json/`.
5. Never cache episode pages (`/episode/…`) or put `/media/` behind a Worker: the first sets each viewer's session, the second skips WordPress's checks.
6. Optional: **Security → WAF → Rate limiting rules**, `/media/` at about 600 requests per minute per IP.

## 8. Install the theme and plugin

1. Download [`wuxia-core.zip`](https://github.com/Wuxia-KH/wuxia-press-published-/releases/latest/download/wuxia-core.zip) and [`wuxia-theme.zip`](https://github.com/Wuxia-KH/wuxia-press-published-/releases/latest/download/wuxia-theme.zip).
2. **Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin** → `wuxia-core.zip` → **Activate**.
3. **Appearance → Themes → Add New Theme → Upload Theme** → `wuxia-theme.zip` → **Activate**.
4. **Settings → Permalinks** → **Post name** → **Save**.
5. Recommended, **before adding storage**: give stored credentials their own key. Add to `wp-config.php`, above `/* That's all, stop editing! */`:

   ```php
   define( 'WUXIA_MEDIA_KEY', 'PASTE_64_RANDOM_CHARACTERS' );
   ```

   Make one with `openssl rand -hex 32`. Back it up with the database: if it is lost or changed, storage credentials must be entered again. Without it, the site's WordPress salts are used.
6. Optional, for password-reset and notification mail through an SMTP relay (Brevo, Mailgun, …), also in `wp-config.php`:

   ```php
   define( 'WUXIA_SMTP_HOST', 'smtp-relay.brevo.com' );
   define( 'WUXIA_SMTP_PORT', '587' );
   define( 'WUXIA_SMTP_USER', 'YOUR_SMTP_LOGIN' );
   define( 'WUXIA_SMTP_PASS', 'YOUR_SMTP_KEY' );
   define( 'WUXIA_MAIL_FROM', 'no-reply@YOUR_DOMAIN' );
   ```

7. **Drama Manager → Storage Providers**: connect your storage. **Drama Manager → Import**: upload iVault JSON, or **Add drama**. **Drama Manager → Settings**: Khmer or English.

## 9. Check that video plays

1. Open any episode and press play.
2. Open the browser's developer tools → **Network**, filter `media`.
3. `master.m3u8` and the segment files (`.ts`, `.m4s`, `.single`, `.married`) must answer **200**.
4. Click a segment: its response headers include `x-wuxia-origin-cache: MISS` the first time and `HIT` after, so nginx's cache works.

From a terminal, a quick check that the rules are in place (any episode number works; a bad link is expected):

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://YOUR_DOMAIN/media/1/0.AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA/master.m3u8
```

`403` or `404` means the rules are working. **`501` means they are not** (see below).

## 10. Troubleshooting

| You see | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `501` "Media is served through nginx" | The request reached WordPress without the media rules. | Add part 2 to the site's `server { }` and reload nginx. On Apache or LiteSpeed hosting this cannot be fixed; move to nginx. |
| `nginx -t`: *"proxy_cache" zone "wuxia_media" is unknown* | Part 1 is missing. | Add part 1 inside `http { }`. |
| `nginx -t`: *"limit_req_zone" directive is not allowed here* | Part 1 was put inside `server { }`. | Move it to `http { }`. |
| Episodes fail and the error log says *Permission denied* under `/var/cache/nginx/wuxia` | nginx's workers can't write the cache folder. | `sudo chown -R www-data /var/cache/nginx/wuxia` (`nginx` on RHEL-family systems), then reload nginx. |
| `502` on every media request, and nginx's error log says *connect() to unix:… failed* | `fastcgi_pass` in part 2 doesn't match your PHP. | Copy the value from your `location ~ \.php$` block. `ls /run/php/` lists the sockets. |
| `502` "Storage did not answer" | nginx couldn't reach your storage. | Check the provider in **Storage Providers**. The error log may say *could not be resolved* (the `resolver` line) or *certificate verify failed* (the CA-bundle line). |
| `503` "Storage is busy" | Telegram asked to slow down. | It retries by itself. |
| `403` "This link has expired" | Media links last six hours. | Reload the page. |
| `404` | That episode or file doesn't exist. | Check the episode's link and provider. |
| `429` | Too many requests from one IP. | Behind Cloudflare, do step [2.5](#25-nginx-visitor-ips-behind-cloudflare) so viewers aren't counted as one. |
| wp-admin loops "too many redirects" | Cloudflare SSL is *Flexible*. | Set **Full (strict)** with the origin certificate. |
| Path D: Nginx Proxy Manager shows *502 Bad Gateway* | It can't reach the `web` container. | `sudo docker compose ps`: all four services must be up. The proxy host forwards to `web`, port `80`, scheme `http`. |
| Path D: the certificate request fails | Let's Encrypt couldn't check the domain. | The domain must already point at the server. Behind Cloudflare's orange cloud, use **Use a DNS Challenge** with a Cloudflare API token. |
| Path D: `501` although everything runs | `site.conf` or the split media files are missing. | In `~/wuxia`, `ls nginx` must list the five files from step 5.2; then `sudo docker compose restart web`. |
| Episode pages or `/shorts/` answer 404 | Permalinks are "Plain". | **Settings → Permalinks → Post name → Save**. |

nginx's error log is `/var/log/nginx/error.log`; media requests are also in the access log. On Path D: `sudo docker compose logs web` (and `logs npm` for the proxy).

## 11. Updates and backups

- **Update**: download the new zips and upload them the same way; WordPress asks to replace the installed version. Every release lists `SHA256SUMS`. Check each release's notes for a new `nginx-wuxia-media.conf`.
- **Replaced a video at the same address?** Empty nginx's cache or it keeps the old copy for up to 7 days: `sudo rm -rf /var/cache/nginx/wuxia/*` (Path D: `sudo docker compose exec web sh -c 'rm -rf /var/cache/nginx/wuxia/*'`)
- **Path D, updating the containers**: `cd ~/wuxia && sudo docker compose pull && sudo docker compose up -d`
- **Back up** the database and `wp-config.php` (it holds `WUXIA_MEDIA_KEY`; on Path D, `docker-compose.yml`) every day, and keep a copy off the server. Path D: `sudo docker compose exec -T db sh -c 'mariadb-dump -uroot -p"$MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD" wuxia' | gzip > ~/wuxia-$(date +%F).sql.gz`. Paths A to C:

  ```bash
  sudo mysqldump --single-transaction wuxia | gzip > ~/wuxia-$(date +%F).sql.gz
  ```

---

## File: server/nginx-wuxia-media.conf

```
# Wuxia video playback for nginx (any nginx server, no Docker needed).
#
# Why: the plugin never lets PHP stream video. WordPress checks each signed
# /media/ link and names the real file; nginx fetches it from your storage and
# streams it, keeping the storage address and credentials hidden. Without these
# rules every episode answers "501 Media is served through nginx".
#
# Apache, LiteSpeed and most shared hosting cannot run this. There the pages
# work but episodes do not play; use a server (or VPS) with nginx.
#
# How: put PART 1 inside `http { }` (for example /etc/nginx/conf.d/wuxia.conf)
# and PART 2 inside your site's `server { }`, next to its other locations.
# Change the two lines marked CHANGE, then: sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
#
# Check: open an episode; in the browser's Network tab its .m3u8 and .ts files
# answer 200 (403 "expired" after six hours is normal: reload the page).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- PART 1: http { }

# A viewer fetches a segment every few seconds; seeking fetches a few at once.
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=wuxia_media_rate:10m rate=30r/s;

# Each storage file once on this server's disk, shared by every viewer. Size it
# to your disk (20g is about 50 hours of 720p); unused files go after 7 days.
# The folder must exist and belong to nginx's user:
#   sudo mkdir -p /var/cache/nginx/wuxia && sudo chown -R www-data /var/cache/nginx/wuxia
proxy_cache_path /var/cache/nginx/wuxia levels=1:2 keys_zone=wuxia_media:50m
                 max_size=20g inactive=7d use_temp_path=off;

# -------------------------------------------------------------- PART 2: server { }

# WordPress answers every /media/ request (the flag below tells the plugin
# nginx is in front); for video files it hands the fetch back to nginx.
location ^~ /media/ {
	limit_req zone=wuxia_media_rate burst=80 nodelay;
	limit_req_status 429;
	include fastcgi_params;
	fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $document_root/index.php;
	fastcgi_param SCRIPT_NAME /index.php;
	fastcgi_param WUXIA_MEDIA_ACCEL 1;
	# CHANGE: the same fastcgi_pass as your site's `location ~ \.php$` block,
	# e.g. unix:/run/php/php8.3-fpm.sock or 127.0.0.1:9000
	fastcgi_pass unix:/run/php/php8.3-fpm.sock;
}

# Reachable only from the location above (X-Accel-Redirect). The storage
# address and credentials come from WordPress in response headers and never
# reach the viewer; the viewer's own headers are not sent to storage.
location = /_wuxia_upstream {
	internal;
	set $wuxia_from_php $upstream_http_x_wuxia_key;
	if ($wuxia_from_php) {
		set $wuxia_url   $upstream_http_x_wuxia_url;
		set $wuxia_auth  $upstream_http_x_wuxia_auth;
		set $wuxia_cache $upstream_http_x_wuxia_cache;
		set $wuxia_key   $upstream_http_x_wuxia_key;
	}

	proxy_cache wuxia_media;
	proxy_cache_key $wuxia_key;
	proxy_cache_valid 200 7d;
	proxy_cache_valid 404 1m;
	proxy_cache_lock on;
	proxy_cache_lock_timeout 15s;
	proxy_cache_use_stale error timeout updating http_500 http_502 http_503 http_504;
	proxy_cache_background_update on;
	proxy_ignore_headers Cache-Control Expires Set-Cookie Vary X-Accel-Expires;

	# nginx looks up storage hosts itself; any public DNS resolver works.
	resolver 1.1.1.1 8.8.8.8 valid=300s ipv6=off;
	resolver_timeout 5s;
	proxy_pass $wuxia_url;
	proxy_http_version 1.1;
	proxy_ssl_server_name on;
	proxy_ssl_verify on;
	# CHANGE on RHEL/Alma/Rocky: /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt
	proxy_ssl_trusted_certificate /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt;
	proxy_ssl_verify_depth 3;
	proxy_connect_timeout 5s;
	proxy_read_timeout 30s;

	proxy_pass_request_headers off;
	proxy_set_header Authorization $wuxia_auth;
	proxy_set_header User-Agent "wuxia-media";

	# Nothing about the storage behind reaches the viewer.
	proxy_hide_header Set-Cookie;
	proxy_hide_header Cache-Control;
	proxy_hide_header Expires;
	proxy_hide_header Content-Disposition;
	proxy_hide_header Access-Control-Allow-Origin;
	proxy_hide_header Via;
	proxy_hide_header X-Cache;
	proxy_hide_header X-Served-By;
	proxy_hide_header X-Timer;
	proxy_hide_header X-Jsd-Version;
	proxy_hide_header X-Jsd-Version-Type;
	proxy_hide_header Fastly-Restarts;
	proxy_hide_header X-GitHub-Request-Id;
	proxy_hide_header X-Amz-Request-Id;
	proxy_hide_header X-Amz-Id-2;
	proxy_hide_header Cf-Ray;
	proxy_hide_header Alt-Svc;
	proxy_hide_header Strict-Transport-Security;
	proxy_hide_header Report-To;
	proxy_hide_header Nel;
	proxy_hide_header Timing-Allow-Origin;
	proxy_hide_header X-Content-Type-Options;
	proxy_hide_header Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy;
	proxy_hide_header Access-Control-Expose-Headers;

	add_header Cache-Control $wuxia_cache always;
	add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
	add_header Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy "same-origin" always;
	add_header Content-Disposition "inline" always;
	add_header X-Robots-Tag "noindex, nofollow" always;
	add_header X-Wuxia-Origin-Cache $upstream_cache_status always;
}
```

---

## File: server/nginx-proxy-manager/docker-compose.yml

```
# Wuxia for WordPress behind Nginx Proxy Manager: Path D of the deployment guide,
# https://wuxia-kh.github.io/wuxia-press-published-/deploy.html#path-d
#
# Replace A_STRONG_DB_PASSWORD and A_STRONG_ROOT_PASSWORD (the guide does it
# with one command), then: docker compose up -d

services:
  # Nginx Proxy Manager: the only thing the internet reaches. HTTPS
  # certificates, and the admin panel on port 81.
  npm:
    image: jc21/nginx-proxy-manager:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
      # The admin panel: only on this server. Reach it through an SSH tunnel
      # (see the guide); never open it to the internet.
      - "127.0.0.1:81:81"
    volumes:
      - ./npm/data:/data
      - ./npm/letsencrypt:/etc/letsencrypt

  db:
    image: mariadb:11
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MARIADB_DATABASE: wuxia
      MARIADB_USER: wuxia
      MARIADB_PASSWORD: A_STRONG_DB_PASSWORD
      MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD: A_STRONG_ROOT_PASSWORD
    volumes:
      - db:/var/lib/mysql

  # WordPress as PHP-FPM: no web server of its own.
  wordpress:
    image: wordpress:php8.3-fpm
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: [db]
    environment:
      WORDPRESS_DB_HOST: db
      WORDPRESS_DB_NAME: wuxia
      WORDPRESS_DB_USER: wuxia
      WORDPRESS_DB_PASSWORD: A_STRONG_DB_PASSWORD
      # Nginx Proxy Manager ends HTTPS; tell WordPress the visitor used it.
      WORDPRESS_CONFIG_EXTRA: |
        if ( ( $$_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO'] ?? '' ) === 'https' ) { $$_SERVER['HTTPS'] = 'on'; }
    volumes:
      - wp:/var/www/html

  # nginx with the Wuxia media rules, between the proxy and WordPress.
  web:
    image: nginx:stable
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: [wordpress]
    volumes:
      - wp:/var/www/html:ro
      - ./nginx/site.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro
      - ./nginx/wuxia-media-http.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/wuxia-media-http.conf:ro
      - ./nginx/cloudflare.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/cloudflare.conf:ro
      - ./nginx/wuxia-media-server.conf:/etc/nginx/snippets/wuxia-media-server.conf:ro
      - media_cache:/var/cache/nginx/wuxia

volumes:
  db:
  wp:
  media_cache:
```

---

## File: server/nginx-proxy-manager/nginx/site.conf

```
# The nginx between Nginx Proxy Manager and WordPress: it serves the site and
# carries the Wuxia media rules (snippets/wuxia-media-server.conf).
# Path D of the Wuxia for WordPress deployment guide.

# Behind Nginx Proxy Manager: the visitor's address arrives in X-Forwarded-For.
# Trust it only from Docker's private network (the proxy).
set_real_ip_from 172.16.0.0/12;
set_real_ip_from 10.0.0.0/8;
set_real_ip_from 192.168.0.0/16;
real_ip_header X-Forwarded-For;
real_ip_recursive on;

server {
	listen 80;
	server_name _;
	root /var/www/html;
	index index.php;
	client_max_body_size 64m;
	server_tokens off;

	# Video (Wuxia). Its ^~ locations take priority over the rules below.
	include snippets/wuxia-media-server.conf;

	location ~ /\. { deny all; }
	location = /xmlrpc.php { deny all; }
	location ~* ^/wp-content/uploads/.*\.php$ { deny all; }

	location / {
		try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?$args;
	}

	location ~ \.php$ {
		try_files $uri =404;
		include fastcgi_params;
		fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $document_root$fastcgi_script_name;
		fastcgi_pass wordpress:9000;
	}

	location ~* \.(css|js|webp|avif|jpg|jpeg|png|svg|ttf|woff2)$ {
		expires 30d;
		access_log off;
	}
}
```
